subject: Private deployment: upgrade alignment and rollback triggers

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: AcmeBank Security <security@acmebank.com>, AcmeBank Ops Lead <ops-lead@acmebank.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment: upgrade alignment and rollback triggers

Hi team —

We promised AcmeBank a clear, low-risk plan for the upcoming Private runtime patch (v3.1.2 -> v3.2.0). This thread is to align on: scope, maintenance window options, pin-and-fallback mechanics, and the specific rollback triggers that will cause an immediate unpin.

Summary (high level):
- Target change: runtime + kernel updates, security backports, and a minor model artifact format change.
- Proposed window: Saturday 2026-11-06 02:00–06:00 UTC (US regions) — optional second wave for APAC if needed.
- Pin strategy: host-level pin for current production model (pinned to v3.1.2) for read-only until successful validation; traffic shifted to v3.2.0 for canary subset.
- Rollback triggers (draft): error rate > 1.5% on 2 consecutive minutes, median tail latency >2.5x baseline for >5 minutes, or any customer-reported data corruption.

Irene and Karthik will provide a short technical note on the operational steps and KV cache evacuation. Acme: please confirm the acceptable maintenance window, your preferred SLA for the permit-to-failover decision, and any additional audit evidence you need.

Attachments: initial playbook (draft) attached.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Principal Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private deployment: upgrade alignment and rollback triggers

Thanks Jordan — quick technical addendum below.

Operational notes (concise):
- Canary sizing: 5% traffic to 2 dedicated canary nodes (isolated pool). If canary passes 30m validation (error rate <0.3% and latency within 1.2x baseline), we scale to 25% for a further 45m.
- KV cache: we'll snapshot and warm the canary with recent KV prefixes. If cache warm failure occurs, routing will fallback to pinned nodes; that is NOT an automatic rollback unless error rates spike.
- Model artifact change: format change requires a one-time KV migration step that is idempotent; we will run migration in preflight on staging and prod-shadow first.
- Rollback automation: we have two levels — soft abort (halt further rollouts and notify) and hard revert (automatic traffic shift back to pinned nodes + emergency unpin).

Hard revert triggers (proposal):
1) Any customer-facing data corruption incident (manual/unambiguous).
2) 2-minute sustained error rate > 1.5% AND absolute error count > 50.
3) ≥30% increase in 95th percentile latency over baseline for >10 minutes.

Operational checklist included in the attached playbook section 3.4.

Irene
Irene Choi
Staff Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Jordan — thanks for the clear note. A few requests from AcmeBank security & ops before we sign off on the window:

1) Evidence/artifacts: we need the preflight test matrix and a copy of the staging run logs for the KV migration. Please provide the exact Drive link and a short explanation of failure modes you observed in staging.
2) Audit trail: during rollback we require immutable audit entries for the following events: pin-off, traffic-shift, canary-pass, canary-fail, and emergency-unpin. Is that exportable to our SIEM?
3) RTO expectation: if we hit a hard revert trigger, what is the expected median time-to-restore (TTR) for customer traffic to be on pinned nodes? We need a guaranteed median TTR ≤ 7 minutes in the SLA for this wave.

Also: can you confirm whether the kernel updates require a driver restart that would impact host-level connections (we prefer no forced driver restarts during the window).

We'll block the proposed Saturday window tentatively; final signoff once artifacts + SLAs are confirmed.

Regards,
Acme Security
--
AcmeBank Security Team

Subject: Re: Private deployment: upgrade alignment and rollback triggers

Acme team — thanks, good questions. Answers inline and next steps below.

1) Evidence/artifacts: staging run logs and the preflight matrix are uploaded here: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/upgrade-playbooks/ACMEBank (shared). The ZIP contains the log excerpts for the KV migration (staging-run-2026-10-09.tar.gz) and the preflight checklist. No blocked failures observed in staging; two transient cache warm warnings (documented).

2) Audit trail: yes — every state transition (pin-off, traffic-shift, canary-pass/fail, emergency-unpin) is written to the audit log as an append-only entry and exported via the SIEM connector. I've attached the audit export spec we will push to your SIEM endpoint.

3) RTO expectation: with the current routing components and warm caches, median TTR for hard revert is 4–6 minutes (we estimate 95th percentile < 10 minutes). We will include a contractual SLA clause with median TTR ≤ 7 minutes for this wave only.

Driver restart: the kernel updates are in-userland drivers and do NOT require a full hardware driver restart. We expect no host-level disconnects; we'll still run a small canary to validate.

Next steps / ask list: 
- Acme: confirm you are okay with the Saturday window (2026-11-06 02:00–06:00 UTC).
- Security: confirm the SIEM endpoint for audit exports and any field mapping you need.
- SRE (Irene/Karthik): please finalize the hard revert exact metric thresholds; I'll loop legal for the narrow SLA addendum.

Attached: playbook v1, and Acme checklist (as requested).

Jordan
Principal Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
